claims.text: The initial nanoparticles are solid, equimolar Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy alloys.
The initial Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles form a single-phase solid solution.
Limited atomic mobility preserves local compositional fluctuations in the solid nanoparticles.
Local compositional fluctuations create nanoscale regions with lower melting points.
The lower-melting regions cause premature surface premelting relative to homogeneous nanoparticles.
The proposed intervention is controlled heating through the premelting and melting ranges with in situ characterization and stochastic modeling.
The comparison will hold particle size, defect density, and heating rate approximately constant.
The proposed particles are smaller than approximately 10 nm.
Single-metal nanoparticles or well-homogenized alloy nanoparticles are proposed as baselines under the same thermal protocol.
Limited mobility maintains local compositional fluctuations at nanoparticle surfaces.
The compositional fluctuations produce segregated surface microdomains.
Insufficient atomic diffusion during heating prevents complete homogenization of the HEA nanoparticles.
Surface microdomains melt before the nanoparticle bulk because their local melting points are reduced.
Homogeneous baseline nanoparticles melt uniformly at a single well-defined temperature.
The HEA nanoparticles will exhibit localized surface premelting below their bulk melting point.
The HEA nanoparticles will display spatially heterogeneous melting fronts.
Baseline nanoparticles have higher effective atomic mobility than the proposed HEA nanoparticles.
The mechanism should be most important in small particles produced under conditions that do not promote complete atomic mixing.
The mechanism may cease to apply for substantially larger particles or after thermal treatment permits significant diffusion.

Absence of significantly earlier or spatially heterogeneous premelting relative to the homogeneous baseline, or absence of correlation between mobility and compositional variation, would falsify the hypothesis.
